title: Pool Health Scenario Wizard for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design a guided 'Scenario Wizard' in Redwood Console that lets operators model GPU pool health and autoscale/burst settings against historical and synthetic traffic. The wizard produces recommended profiles and a preview of cost/latency trade-offs before committing settings to a pool.
background: Operators managing dedicated GPU pools currently switch between multiple views (health graphs, autoscale config, cost estimates) and manually reconcile them. This causes configuration churn and hesitation during incidents. Research interviews (5 platform engineers) highlighted the need to simulate outcomes before changing autoscale/burst policies.
goals: 1) Reduce time-to-safe-config by providing a clear simulation and recommendations. 2) Surface health-driven autoscale presets and burst budgets. 3) Show immediate cost and latency impacts of policy changes. 4) Make committing config a clear, auditable step tied to rollout policies.
scope: Wizard UI (stepper) + one-click apply to pool + dry-run simulation modal + revised cost card in pool header. Does NOT include backend autoscaler logic changes or quota enforcement; those require separate ENG tickets.
success_metrics: Median time to change autoscale config reduced by 40%
Number of rollbacks after config changes reduced by 30%
>70% of operators use recommended preset at least once
design_notes: Wizard is a 4-step modal: 1) Baseline (select pool + timeframe), 2) Load profile (historical / synthetic / spike simulation), 3) Policy builder (presets + manual), 4) Preview & audit (cost/latency forecast + rollout options). Use compact graphs to avoid information overload. Include a toggle for conservative vs aggressive cost modes.
decisions: Use a modal stepper anchored to pool header for minimal navigation friction
Expose 3 recommended presets derived from heuristics: 'Conservative', 'Balanced', 'Aggressive'
Preview uses a 95th-percentile latency forecast and an estimated hourly cost delta
tradeoffs: Favoring clarity over exposing every autoscaler knob; advanced tuning will remain in the expanded Autoscale page. Simulation accuracy depends on backend sampling and may be optimistic for synthetic spike tests—include explicit confidence bands.
review_comments: PM (Lina Park): Add a 'rollback to previous config' CTA on the apply confirmation
ENG (Ravi Patel): Need a dry-run API to return cost/latency projections, flagged as approximation
Security (Marta Ruiz): Ensure audit log entry includes the sim parameters and user id
acceptance_criteria: Wizard flows implemented in Figma and validated in hallway usability tests (n=6)
Console shows cost delta and latency forecast in preview modal
Apply path creates an auditable change event visible in pool's activity feed
QA smoke tests for modal open/close, sims run, and apply/rollback flows
next_steps: Design: finalize microcopy and empty states (due 2026-03-16)
PM: schedule canary rollout with 2 pilot pools (PM-4210)
Create UX acceptance test checklist and handoff package
notes_for_engineering: Sim output must include: projected 95th latency, projected avg token cost, estimated GPU-hours consumed. Provide a confidence score and origin (historical/synthetic). Endpoint should accept pool_id, timeframe, and synthetic load pattern. UI will treat projections as advisory only.
usability_findings: Prototype testing revealed confusion around 'burst budget' labeling; users preferred 'Burst capacity (GPU-minutes)' and asked for a slider with exact GPU-minutes value. Also requested a quick comparison card showing 'current vs proposed' key metrics.
communication_plan: Post-merge announcement in #console-release with link to doc and how-to GIF; include sample rollback command for platform teams; update Console help center with 'How to simulate pool changes' article.
